Definition: Whether the system enables Know Your Customer (KYC) packet collection for service provision, particularly financial services
Comments: The national identity card is accepted for Know Your Customer (KYC) processes in banking and financial services. Banks and non-bank financial institutions (45,000 accounts per the World Bank diagnostic) require KYC using ID documents including the CNI. However, there is no digital KYC infrastructure; verification is manual/physical only. Mobile money (Orange) also uses ID for registration.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. CEMAC/BEAC-COBAC AML-KYC regulation (Loi n°08.012, 2008) requires CAR banks and microfinance institutions to verify client identity via official documents (national ID, passport, residence permit) before opening accounts, corroborating manual, document-based KYC. Note the original World Bank ID4D diagnostic is actually a 2017 report (not 2023 as labelled) — content is dated but the core finding (paper-based KYC, no digital infrastructure) still holds; no evidence of eKYC/API-based verification found. Value code unchanged at 2 (Yes).

Definition: Whether national data protection legislation exists and covers personal data linked to the ID system
Comments: Law No. 24.001 on the Protection of Personal Data was enacted in January 2024. The law establishes comprehensive data protection principles (lawfulness, transparency, purpose limitation, storage limitation), regulates sensitive data including biometric data, provides data subject rights (access, rectification, erasure), and requires a Data Protection Officer. It mandates the creation of an independent supervisory authority within 12 months of enactment.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed and strongly corroborated. The primary legal text (Loi n°24.001, January 2024) explicitly classifies biometric and genetic data as sensitive data subject to stricter processing rules, and independent trackers (Data Protection Africa, ConsentStack) confirm the law's enactment date and scope. Note the mandated independent supervisory authority missed its January 2025 establishment deadline and the Ministry of Digital Economy is acting as interim overseer — relevant to the separate 'DPA Oversight' variable, not to this one. Value code unchanged at 2 (Yes).

Definition: Whether the Ministry of Finance has oversight of the financing and development of the digital ID system
Comments: Partial oversight. The Directorate General of Public Procurement (under the Ministry of Finance and Budget) formally objected in 2018 to the Al-Madina contract for non-compliance with procurement laws. The Finance Law sets the official CNI price at CFA 4,500. However, revenues from ID card issuance have reportedly not been appearing in the state budget, suggesting limited effective financial control over the ID system.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed, with stronger and fresher evidence of weak enforcement. Radio Ndeke Luka (2022) and abangui.com report that Al Madina continued charging CFA 6,750 for the CNI against the statutory CFA 4,500 price nearly two years after a 2020 administrative tribunal annulled the increase, and that ID-card revenues do not appear as a distinct budget line (only ~8 million CFA/year recorded against an implied much higher volume of cards issued), with Finance Ministry unable to say where the funds go. This confirms the Ministry of Finance sets nominal price controls (a form of oversight) but cannot enforce them — consistent with 'partial' rather than 'full' oversight, and arguably close to the 'no effective oversight' end of that band. Value code unchanged at 2 (Partial oversight), but flagged that this is weak/nominal oversight in practice.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for accessing public healthcare services
Comments: Identity documents are accepted but not mandatory for healthcare access. The Ministry of Health uses identity for records, and hospitals issue birth attestations (55% of births occur in health facilities). Health services are generally accessible without strict ID requirements given the humanitarian context. No evidence of mandatory ID-linked healthcare access found.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Not independently corroborated — recommend human review. The cited World Bank source is in fact an ID4D diagnostic dated 2017 (not 2023 as labelled in this dataset), and I could not verify its specific claims on ID use in healthcare in the fetched text. Fresh searches found that targeted free care (children under 5, pregnant/breastfeeding women, GBV victims) is governed by Decree n°19.032 (2019) and a new national health insurance fund (CNAM, validated October 2025) is being rolled out for civil servants first — neither source discusses an ID-card requirement for accessing care. No authoritative source found confirming or contradicting whether a credential is 'accepted but not mandatory' versus simply not used at all. Value code left at 2 pending human review; evidence base is weak and dated.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for SIM card activation and mobile service registration
Comments: SIM card registration with ID is accepted (not mandatory in the strictest enforcement sense but required by regulation). Decision 018/MPTNT/CMAJ/09 (2009) required SIM card registration with a valid ID. A 2017 decision mandated inactivation of unregistered SIMs. The World Bank noted 1.185 million subscribers with 20–30% churn and high verification costs. Non-biometric ID registration applies.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Changed from 2 to 3 (Mandatory). Privacy International's SIM registration tracker (citing GSMA data, current to 2021) explicitly lists the Central African Republic among countries with mandatory SIM card registration laws. The Paradigm/Londa Digital Rights in Africa report (2022) confirms this is codified in Article 61 of the Electronic Communications Law of 2018 ('Operators are obliged to identify all subscribers of their services'), which supersedes the 2009 decision cited in the original comment. UNHCR's 'Displaced and Disconnected' country report also states SIM registration 'is required by law' in CAR. This is a legal mandate, not merely an accepted option, so the score is raised to Mandatory.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for registering for social assistance programs and accessing social services
Comments: Identity documents are accepted (not universally mandatory) for social services. The Ministry of Social Affairs and National Reconciliation (MASRN) and humanitarian agencies (WFP, UNICEF) use identity for beneficiary identification in cash transfer and social protection programs. The World Bank ID4D diagnostic noted social protection programs (PACAD, LONDO) covering 190,000 and 35,500 beneficiaries respectively. The lack of widespread ID coverage is a key barrier to inclusive social protection delivery.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Corroborated but ambiguous — recommend human review before changing. UNOPS reporting on the World Bank-funded PACAD cash-transfer programme (45,000+ households) states 'every recipient must show an identity card and provide their fingerprints before receiving a payment', which reads as closer to mandatory than merely accepted for that programme. However, it is unclear from available sources whether this is the national CNI/digital ID specifically or a project-issued beneficiary card (PACAD/LONDO both use community-based targeting and their own biometric enrolment for the Rapid Social Registry), so I cannot confidently reclassify to Mandatory. Beneficiary figures in the original comment (PACAD 190,000) also do not match the fresher project documents (PACAD ~244,525 individuals/45,000 households; LONDO 35,500 direct beneficiaries, confirmed). Value code left at 2 pending clarification of which credential is actually required.
